propositions: Comment triage of scoped files (store, reducer, graph, snapshot) cannot recover meaningful line count from two size-pressured files: event_append.py (791/800 lines) and _processors.py (777/800 lines) because their comments encode load-bearing replay-compatibility and migration-guard rationales that must not be relocated.

Multiple verified-stale comments document live runtime behavior and must be corrected in place rather than deleted: gitutil.py incorrectly claims no rebar imports despite a deferred in-function import; hlc.py's kill-switch description is outdated by four schema bumps; llm_format.py header cites a stale package path and omits four live key maps.

The reducer/_processors.py:719-774 snapshot-restore migration guards are highest-risk for relocation: their comments warn that removing certain guards would cause live production breakage (channel clobbering with 'unknown'), and these rationales must remain verbatim in code.

A two-homes changelog exists (reducer/_version.py:39-66 and docs/event-schema.md) with docs partial and stale (missing v4/v5); canonical content must be consolidated into docs before the code copy is reduced to a one-line citation.

The negative result stands: comment triage recovers only ~31 net lines across the scope by removing duplicates and relocating non-load-bearing rationales, leaving the two size-pressured files essentially unchanged.
